title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: SME manpower cost difficulties
sections.summary: A November survey found the share of SMEs with manpower cost difficulties fell from a peak of 85% to below 72%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the survey finding which was released in November last year, the proportion of SMEs experiencing difficulties with manpower costs fell from its peak of 85% to pre-2012 level of below 72%.

sections.label: Professional Conversion Programme placements
sections.summary: Last year the Professional Conversion Programme helped more than 3,700 mid-career individuals take up new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Last year, the Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) helped more than 3,700 mid-career individuals take up new jobs.

sections.label: Productivity Solution Grant streamlining
sections.summary: Existing grants for pre-scoped, off-the-shelf technologies will be streamlined into a single Productivity Solution Grant funding up to 70% of qualifying costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Among others, existing grants that support the adoption of pre-scoped, off-the-shelf technologies will be streamlined into a single Productivity Solution Grant (PSG) where the Government will provide funding for up to 70% of the qualifying costs.

sections.label: NRF-Temasek IP Commercialisation Vehicle
sections.summary: This year's Budget announced a $100 million NRF-Temasek IP Commercialisation Vehicle to provide equity funding for tech startups using publicly funded research IP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To provide equity funding for cutting-edge tech startups that draw on intellectual property (IP) generated from publicly funded research, this year's Budget announced the setting up of the $100 million National Research Foundation (NRF)-Temasek IP Commercialisation Vehicle.

sections.label: SME Go Digital and TeSA
sections.summary: The SME Go Digital Programme launched in 2017 and the Tech Skills Accelerator launched in 2016 are flagship programmes helping businesses and individuals develop digital capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The SME Go Digital Programme was launched in 2017 and the Tech Skills Accelerator (TeSA) launched in 2016 are both flagship programmes assisting businesses and individuals to develop digital capabilities.

sections.label: Single PACT scheme
sections.summary: This year's Budget consolidated EDB's and SPRING Singapore's PACT schemes into a single PACT scheme to forge stronger partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With the aim to forge stronger partnerships, this year's Budget also spring cleaned the existing schemes, such as EDB's Partnerships for Capability Transformation (PACT) and SPRING Singapore's PACT, into a single PACT scheme.

sections.label: Update on lifestyle cluster ITMs
sections.summary: The speaker seeks an update from the Minister on progress of ITMs launched over a year ago, including lifestyle cluster ITMs covering food services, food manufacturing, retail and hotels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I would like to seek an update from the Minister on the progress of some of the ITMs that were launched over a year ago, such as the lifestyle cluster ITMs which encompass food services, food manufacturing, retail and hotels.

sections.label: Training relevance and economic growth
sections.summary: The speaker asks how Government works with industry and employers to keep training relevant, noting 2017 GDP growth exceeded expectations and 2018 growth is expected to be moderate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Can I ask how the Government is working with industry and employers to ensure training remains relevant?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the global economy and Singapore economy posted better than expected gross domestic product (GDP) growth rates in 2017, while in 2018, economic growth is expected to be moderate.

sections.label: AEC establishment and Singapore focus
sections.summary: The AEC would be the fourth largest economic bloc, but ASEAN deferred one-fifth of 506 measures to 2025, and Minister Lim Hng Kiang said Singapore will focus on digital economy and trade facilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If integrated as a single market and production base, the AEC will become the fourth largest economic bloc in the world, just behind the United States (US), China and the European Union (EU).

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: AEC was to be established by end of 2015, but ASEAN failed to achieve one-fifth of the 506 measures and had deferred them for 10 years to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In January this year, Minister Lim Hng Kiang said Singapore will focus on the digital economy and trade facilitation.

sections.label: Asian emerging markets growth projection
sections.summary: Growth in Asian emerging markets as a whole is projected to average 6% from 2015 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, growth in Asian emerging markets as a whole is projected to average 6% from 2015 to 2020.

sections.label: ASEAN total trade growth
sections.summary: Since 1993, ASEAN countries have grown their total trade from US$400 billion to US$2.5 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, since 1993, the ASEAN countries have grown their total trade from US$400 billion to US$2.5 trillion.

sections.label: CPTPP recent efforts achievement
sections.summary: Recent efforts on the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) are described as a major achievement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, recent efforts on this Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) is a major achievement.

sections.label: US TPP withdrawal turnaround
sections.summary: The passage states that against the earlier setback of the US withdrawing from the TPP, this is a remarkable turnaround that will strengthen Singapore's reputation as a progressive partner promoting global free trade.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Set against the setback posed earlier by the decision of the US to withdraw from the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), this is a remarkable turnaround that will further strengthen Singapore's reputation as a progressive partner in the movement to promote global free trade.

sections.label: Global free trade consensus
sections.summary: The passage states that the global consensus on free trade is not quite what it used to be.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the global consensus on free trade is not quite what it used to be.

sections.label: Minister's perspective on FTAs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can share the Government's perspective on FTAs in the emerging new normal of global politics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Given this shifting environment, can the Minister share the Government’s perspective on FTAs in this emerging new normal of global politics?

sections.label: WTO deals and fallback strategies
sections.summary: The passage asks about prospects for further WTO deals and what fallback strategies are being built into trade links for a trade war between major economies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Likewise, what are the prospects for further World Trade Organization (WTO) deals in this new environment?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And even as we hope for the best of outcomes around the world, what fallback strategies are we building into our trade links to maximise Singapore's manoeuvring room in the event of an unfortunate trade war between any of the major economies?

sections.label: MTI strategy for competitiveness
sections.summary: The passage asks what MTI's strategy is to help Singapore and Singapore companies remain competitive to support economic growth and create opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: More broadly, what is MTI's strategy to help Singapore and Singapore companies remain competitive to support economic growth sustainably in the years ahead to create opportunities for Singapore and Singaporeans from all walks of life?

sections.label: Grants and schemes for companies
sections.summary: The passage states the Government has been assisting companies, especially SMEs, through grants and schemes, and with ESG many will be integrated into one single grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: The Government has been assisting companies, especially SMEs, at their different stages of development through grants and schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: And with ESG, many of these grants and schemes will be integrated into one single grant.

sections.label: EDG, CDG, GCP grants integration
sections.summary: EDG is set up and integrated with CDG and GCP grants, with claims only after project completion, and a request for advance payments to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Hopefully, with the setting up of EDG, and integrating it with the different grants of CDG and GCP is a step in the right direction to be more stringent in the process of tightening this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Submission of claim for a grant can only be made after a project is completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: We would like to request that it will be helpful to some of the SMEs that once the grant is approved, that there will be an initial advance payment to the SMEs to help them.

sections.label: Partnership schemes and business succession
sections.summary: Partnership schemes will be streamlined into one, and MTI confirmed schemes support consulting for family business succession planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: It is not in the area of just volumes of business, but it is in the area of services, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: It is good to know that the different partnership schemes will now be streamlined and integrated into one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, one consequence of an ageing society is that many family businesses face the challenge of business succession planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: And it is a challenge, since some entrepreneurs do not have children or professional employees who would want to take over, or they may have successors in mind but those successors are not yet able enough to take over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: In reply to a previous PQ, MTI confirmed that a number of schemes exist that can be used to support consulting to facilitate the business succession planning process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: This will nudge SMEs to pay more attention to grooming the next tier in their companies.

sections.label: Productivity growth last year
sections.summary: Last year, productivity growth was 4.5%, the highest figure since 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, our productivity growth was 4.5%, the highest figure achieved since 2010.

sections.label: PSG support after approval
sections.summary: After approval, PSG will support 70% of a company's productivity investment and expenses, with the company bearing 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Basically, after approval, PSG will support 70% of the company’s productivity investment and expenses, while the company will only need to bear 30% of the total costs.

sections.label: GCP and CDG combined under EDG
sections.summary: The Budget announced that IE Singapore's GCP grant and SPRING Singapore's CDG would be combined under an all-new EDG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Budget also announced that IE Singapore’s GCP grant and SPRING Singapore’s CDG would be combined under an all-new EDG.

sections.label: DTDI enhancement for internationalisation
sections.summary: From YA 2019, the DTDI will be enhanced, raising expenses qualifying without prior approval from $100,000 to $150,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, to further support firms to internationalise, with effect from year of assessment (YA) 2019, the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation (DTDI) will be enhanced, with the amount of expenses that can qualify for the DTDI without prior approval being raised from $100,000 to $150,000.

sections.label: Businesses benefiting from government assistance
sections.summary: The passage states that businesses can benefit from Government assistance schemes if they pursue excellence and marshal resources and talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Only then can they benefit from the Government assistance schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I sincerely believe that if businesses pursue excellence and strive for perfection, marshal our resources and talent, they can then find the niche for survival and development within this ever-changing marketplace!

sections.label: PACT SME and project numbers
sections.summary: By mid-2016, over 700 SMEs and 130 projects had benefited from PACT since 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: By mid-2016, over 700 SMEs and 130 projects had benefited from PACT since 2010.

sections.label: Keppel Shipyard PACT example
sections.summary: Keppel Shipyard used PACT for a semi-automated system cutting wastage 20% and manpower 15%, short of the 30% target, needing continued funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: Keppel Shipyard gave the example of using PACT to develop a semi-automated system to reduce the operating costs of blasting, cutting wastage by 20% and manpower by 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: This fell short of the target for cutting manpower by 30%, and Keppel Shipyard said continuous funding from PACT was needed to achieve success.

sections.label: Onerous government project prequalifications
sections.summary: Contractors say some prequalifications for Government projects are so onerous that no local contractors or consultants can qualify.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Contractors tell me that some of the prequalifications called for Government projects are so onerous that none of the local contractors or consultants can qualify.

sections.label: Minister invited to share efforts
sections.summary: The passage invites the Minister to share specific efforts and measures to help Singapore companies break into overseas markets, their progress, and benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In the premises, I invite the Minister to share with us on the following: (a) the specific efforts and measures our Government and its economic agencies have taken to help Singapore companies tap on opportunities to break into new markets overseas; (b) an update on the progress of these efforts and measures; and (c) how Singapore companies have benefited from these.

sections.label: Sectoral-based mentorship platform suggestion
sections.summary: The passage suggests setting up a dedicated sectoral-based mentorship platform for successful SME owners who ventured abroad to share processes and motivate other SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Maybe one suggestion is to set up a dedicated sectoral-based mentorship platform, either online-based or otherwise, for successful SME owners who have ventured abroad to share processes and motivate other SMEs beyond the existing PIC efforts.

sections.label: SPRING and IE merger support
sections.summary: Asks how domestically oriented companies will be helped after the SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore merger, and whether they still get upgrading support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the merger of SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore, can the Minister share how these domestically oriented companies will be helped?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will such companies still receive support for essential upgrading efforts?

sections.label: Germany innovation programme evaluation rule
sections.summary: Germany applies an internal rule that innovation programmes with budgets over €50 million are evaluated shortly after ending or at latest every five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Germany applies an internal rule that innovation programmes with a total budget exceeding €50 million have to be evaluated shortly after the end of a programme or, at latest, every five years, and that will be ex-post evaluation.

sections.label: Korean universities patent commercialisation
sections.summary: Korea worked with 30 universities and public research institutes on over 3,000 patents, yielding about 50 transferred inventions and US$3.8 million in royalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Korean government has also been working directly with 30 universities and public research institutes to assess commercial applications of their patents and there are more than 3,000 in all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This has resulted in approximately 50 inventions that are transferred to relevant industries, generating a total of US$3.8 million in royalties.

sections.label: R&D spending and productivity questions
sections.summary: Asks for total R&D spending over the last decade and productivity improvement rates in industries benefiting from that R&D.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is the total spending on R&D in the last decade?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What are the productivity improvement rates in relevant industries benefiting from such R&D over the last decade?

sections.label: Singapore R&D investment growth
sections.summary: R&D investment rose from S$2 billion under the 1991 National Technology Plan to S$19 billion under RIE 2020, with public sector spending at 1% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Investments in R&D have been significant and sustained, increasing steadily from S$2 billion under the 1991 five-year National Technology Plan to S$19 billion under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2020 Plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore continues to maintain public sector R&D spending at 1% of GDP annually.

sections.label: Retail rentals share of SME costs
sections.summary: Retail rentals make up 30% of total business costs for SMEs in Singapore's retail sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Retail rentals make up 30% of total business costs for SMEs in the retail sector in Singapore.

sections.label: SME rental cost concerns survey
sections.summary: A survey of about 2,500 SME respondents found only 13% cited high rental costs as a top 2017 business concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the Ministry said, on the back of a decline in rentals, only 13% of some 2,500 SME respondents in a survey cited high rental costs as one of the top business concerns in 2017.

sections.label: Merging SPRING and IE Singapore
sections.summary: The Government is merging SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore to form ESG, a dedicated agency for enterprise development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The Government is also making the effort to make structural change in its lead agencies, to merge SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore to form a dedicated agency for enterprise development – ESG.

sections.label: Partnering Ministry to assist SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker commits to partner the Ministry to extend assistance to SMEs and strengthen workforce readiness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, we are committed to partner the Ministry to be one of the ground enablers to extend assistance to SMEs on available schemes and to strengthen the readiness of our workforce, especially those on the SME side.

sections.label: SME manpower programmes and ITMs
sections.summary: SMEs can use programmes like Earn and Learn, Professional Conversion and Career Trial, but face understanding sector ITMs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, SMEs can address their manpower and hiring needs through various programmes, such as the Earn and Learn programme, Professional Conversion Programmes and the new Career Trial programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One key challenge that remains for SMEs is how to make sense of the coming ITMs in the various sectors that have been announced.

sections.label: LEAD success under ESG
sections.summary: The speaker asks how successful LEAD has been and how it will work under ESG for trade associations and chambers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: With the ESG coming into place, with the integration of SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore, could I ask the Minister to share how successful LEAD has been and, under ESG as the administrator, how they can continue to work effectively for the trade associations as well as the chambers?

sections.label: Plans for support schemes navigation
sections.summary: The speaker invites the Minister to share plans on helping companies navigate support schemes and understand technological capacity gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: In the premises, I invite the Minister to share with us (a) on any plans to assist companies to navigate the large set of options in support schemes and technology offerings; and (b) on any plans to help companies better understand what they lack in terms of technological capacity and the steps they can take to remedy this.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, according to the January 2018 figures released by EDB, Singapore's overall manufacturing output in 2017 rose by 10.1% and posted its best performance since 2010.

sections.label: Manufacturing at 20% of GDP
sections.summary: The CFE recommended retaining manufacturing at around 20% of GDP, and the MP asks how the Government will support this.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: The Committee on the Future Economy (CFE) recommended that Singapore continue to build a globally competitive manufacturing sector and retain manufacturing at around 20% of GDP over the medium term.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Can the Minister share on how the Government plans to support this recommendation?

sections.label: Workers' skills amid industry changes
sections.summary: The MP asks how the Government ensures workers keep the right skills for existing or new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Given the changes to multiple industries, how is the Government ensuring that workers can continue to possess the right skills in order to keep doing their jobs or take up new jobs that will be created?

sections.label: Startup and fintech support
sections.summary: SPRING and WSG set aside $2.8 million for startups, and MAS announced a fintech hub at 80 Robinson Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: In August, it was announced that SPRING Singapore and Workforce Singapore (WSG) would set aside $2.8 million to groom the next generation of startups in supply chain and logistics and develop related talent and capabilities in SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: Then, in November, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced the establishment of a financial technology (fintech) innovative hub in the heart of the Central Business District (CBD) known as 80 Robinson Road (80RR)Fintechhubsg.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: This is intended to cater for the increasing number of startups in the fintech scene, and MAS reported that we now have more than 400 fintech startups in Singapore.

sections.label: Under-employment masked by unemployment rate
sections.summary: The MP says the 3.1% resident unemployment rate masks under-employment such as PMETs driving for Grab or Uber.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: While our unemployment figures remain relatively low, with the resident unemployment rate of 3.1%, the figure masks under-employment where a PMET with many years of work experience ends up as a Grab or Uber driver.

sections.label: Arbitration clauses in online terms
sections.summary: Research shows companies like Amazon, Microsoft and Shoppee include arbitration clauses in their online standard terms and conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Our research shows that there are several companies, like Amazon, Microsoft and Shoppee, which provide for an arbitration clause in their online standard terms and conditions.

sections.label: SCT and arbitration clause claims
sections.summary: Consumers with claims below $10,000 cannot seek redress through SCT because of the arbitration clause unless both parties agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If they have a dispute with the online vendor of the products which cannot be resolved through mediation, their usual recourse is to apply to SCT to adjudicate their dispute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, when we checked with SCT, we were told that SCT would not hear the claim by consumers because of the arbitration clause, unless both parties agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, consumers with small claims below $10,000 and who have disputes with the online companies, are unable to seek redress through SCT because of the arbitration clause.

sections.label: SCT arbitration clause jurisdiction
sections.summary: Speaker urges MTI to work with MinLaw so arbitration clauses cannot oust SCT jurisdiction for disputes under $10,000 or within SCT jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Since the Minister for Law has said that the SCT Act will be amended, I would urge MTI to work with MinLaw to ensure that this jurisdiction of the SCT cannot be ousted by arbitration clause if the value of the dispute is less than $10,000 or within the jurisdiction of SCT.

sections.label: Global economy 2017 growth
sections.summary: The IMF says the global economy ended 2017 on a firm note with the broadest growth since 2010.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: The global economy ended on a firm note in 2017, posting the broadest growth since 2010, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

sections.label: Singapore 2018 growth forecast
sections.summary: MTI expects Singapore's economy to grow 1.5% to 3.5% in 2018, likely slightly above the middle of that range.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Specifically, MTI expects the Singapore economy to grow by 1.5% to 3.5% in 2018, with growth likely to come in slightly above the middle of the forecast range.

sections.label: Singapore FTAs and tariff savings
sections.summary: Singapore has 22 implemented FTAs and Economic Partnership Agreements with 33 trading partners, giving companies over S$1.1 billion in tariff savings in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Over the years, we have built depth and breadth in our international linkages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We have an extensive network of 22 implemented FTAs and Economic Partnership Agreements with 33 trading partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Our FTAs have helped our companies benefit from tariff savings of over S$1.1 billion in 2016.

sections.label: China-Singapore Southern Transport Corridor
sections.summary: Singapore and China are jointly developing the CCI-STC to improve connectivity between western China and Southeast Asia, with three Singapore companies in two joint ventures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: For instance, Singapore and China have recognised our strong complementarities and are jointly developing the China-Singapore (Chongqing) Connectivity Initiative Southern Transport Corridor (CCI-STC), which aims to improve connectivity between western China and Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Three Singapore companies – Pacific International Lines (PIL), PSA International and YCH Group – have entered into two joint ventures with Chongqing companies to steer the development of the STC projects.

sections.label: ASEAN economy and growth
sections.summary: ASEAN is currently the sixth largest economy in the world and enjoys a steady growth rate of 5%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: ASEAN is currently the sixth largest economy in the world and enjoy a steady growth rate of 5%.

sections.label: ASEAN AEC measures implementation
sections.summary: ASEAN did not achieve all 506 measures in 2015, but 88% of AEC measures have been implemented to date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: It is true that ASEAN did not quite achieve all 506 measures in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We continue to track, monitor and work on the rest of the measures, and I am happy to report that, to date, 88% of the AEC measures have been implemented.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme and ITMs
sections.summary: The S$4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme was announced in Budget 2016, and all 23 ITMs will be rolled out by end of this month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, this focus on internationalisation and innovation is part of our larger industry transformation efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We announced the S$4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme in Budget 2016, recognising that each sector is different and that transformation, coordinated at the sector level, can deliver more targeted results.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Each ITM takes into account the unique circumstances of the sector and customises efforts through the four key pillars of innovation, productivity, jobs and skills, and internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We have launched 22 ITMs to date, and I am happy to inform Mr Liang Eng Hwa that we would have rolled out all 23 ITMs by end of this month.

sections.label: Unit Labour Cost changes by sector
sections.summary: Overall ULC fell 0.3% in 2017, with manufacturing ULC down 8% while accommodation and food services ULC rose 2%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: In 2017, the overall Unit Labour Cost (ULC) for the economy fell by 0.3%, moderating from the 2% increase in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: While manufacturing ULC declined by 8% on the back of strong productivity gains, ULC for some services sectors, such as the accommodation and food services sector, rose by 2% as wage growth outpaced productivity growth.

sections.label: Industrial space prices and rents
sections.summary: Industrial price index fell 16.6% and rental index fell 13.4% from 2014 peaks, with statistics made public for transparency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: With an increase in the supply of land and industrial space, the industrial price index has decreased by 16.6% from its peak in 2014, while the industrial rental index has declined by 13.4% from its peak in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Third, we have also made public the statistics on industrial space prices, rents, as well as occupancy rates to improve transparency and help companies make informed decisions.

sections.label: Economic growth and wage growth outlook
sections.summary: Singapore's economy grew 3.6% in real terms last year, and collective efforts should enable 2% to 3% annual growth over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Over the next decade, our collective efforts should enable us to grow by 2% to 3% per year on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: This is how we can work together to create an economy that can offer sustainable wage growth and good jobs for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Singapore’s economy grew by 3.6% in real terms last year, higher than the 2.4% growth in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This can be attributed in large part to the global economic recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: However, our tripartite partners’ transformation efforts have also made a valuable contribution by enabling our enterprises and workers to benefit from new economic trends.

sections.label: Varying sector economic performance
sections.summary: Although overall economic performance has improved, the outcome varies across sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As Mr Henry Kwek has noted, although our overall economic performance has improved, the outcome varies across sectors.

sections.label: Electronics cluster value-added growth
sections.summary: Electronics cluster saw 24.4% annualised real value-added growth per annum from 2015 to 2017, boosted by semiconductor demand for smartphones and vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Within the manufacturing sector, on the one hand, the electronics cluster saw strong an annualised real value-added (VA) growth of 24.4% per annum (pa) between 2015 and 2017, boosted by robust demand for semiconductors to be used in smartphones and vehicles.

sections.label: Logistics ITM growth targets
sections.summary: The EDB-led Logistics ITM envisages 5% CAGR from 2015 to 2020, $8.3 billion nominal VA in 2020, and 2,000 new PMET jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: A case in point is the Logistics ITM which is led by EDB, which envisages strong growth with a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 5% between 2015 and 2020, leading to a nominal VA of $8.3 billion in 2020, and the creation of 2,000 new PMET jobs between 2015 and 2020.

sections.label: Sector value-added and productivity growth
sections.summary: The sector saw real VA growth of 4.2% per annum and productivity growth of 5.2% in real VA per actual hour worked.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The sector has seen strong real VA growth of 4.2% pa and even stronger productivity growth of 5.2% in terms of real VA per actual hour worked.

sections.label: Hotel manning ratio reduction target
sections.summary: The hotel targets about a 17% reduction in manning ratio while enabling employees to do more value-added jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Altogether, the hotel is targeting a reduction in manning ratio of about 17% while enabling its employees to do more value-added jobs.

sections.label: EDB and SPRING supported projects
sections.summary: To date, EDB and SPRING Singapore have supported about 180 projects, resulting in about 1,000 partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: On Mr Low Thia Kiang and Mr Teo Ser Luck’s query, to date, EDB and SPRING Singapore have supported about 180 projects, which have resulted in about 1,000 partnerships.

sections.label: Integrated PACT Programme funding
sections.summary: $100 million is allocated over the next three years for an integrated PACT Programme bringing EDB and SPRING Singapore programmes together.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In view of these good outcomes, we have allocated $100 million over the next three years for an integrated PACT Programme, in other words, we are bringing the EDB and SPRING Singapore programmes together to support these and more forms of collaboration among enterprises to work and grow together in capability and business development.

sections.label: ESG support for enterprise types
sections.summary: ESG will tailor programmes to different enterprise types, combining SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore capability building and internationalisation functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Micro and small enterprises account for a significant majority, with medium and large enterprises comprising 4% and 1% respectively of the total enterprise base.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The resources and capabilities also vary considerably across this broad enterprise spectrum.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Therefore, ESG will tailor its programmes to the needs of the different types of enterprises, bringing together the capability building and internationalisation functions of SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore.

sections.label: Venture Debt Programme extension
sections.summary: ESG will extend the pilot Venture Debt Programme by three years until March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In addition, I am pleased to announce that ESG will extend the pilot Venture Debt Programme (VDP) by three years till March 2021.

sections.label: Market Readiness Assistance grant extension
sections.summary: The higher 70% MRA grant support will be extended for two more years until 31 March 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) scheme helps companies defray the costs of foraying into new markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We raised the grant support from 50% of qualifying expenses to 70% from 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin would be pleased to note that we will extend this higher grant quantum for a further two years till 31 March 2020.

sections.label: Consolidating CDG and GCP into EDG
sections.summary: CDG and GCP will be consolidated into the EDG in the fourth quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To better support companies like JK Tech scale up, we will consolidate the CDG and GCP into the EDG in the fourth quarter of this year.

sections.label: RIE2020 Plan investment shifts
sections.summary: Under RIE2020, Singapore invests about 1% of GDP in RIE, comparable to other small research-intensive economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Under the RIE2020 Plan, we have made several shifts to harness technology and innovation to meet our national needs and to drive the next phase of economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We invest about 1% of our GDP in RIE, which is comparable to the public spending of other small research-intensive economies.

sections.label: R&D investment outcomes
sections.summary: Government R&D investment catalysed $50.6 billion in BERD from 2006 to 2016, with RSEs rising from 22,000 to over 35,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Government's investment in R&D has catalysed Business Expenditure on R&D (BERD) of $50.6 billion from 2006 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Both foreign and, increasingly, local companies have recognised Singapore's R&D value proposition and taken steps to deepen their R&D capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This has also led to the creation of good jobs, with the number of Research Scientists and Engineers (RSEs) increasing from 22,000 in 2006 to more than 35,000 in 2016.

sections.label: Singapore Bloomberg Innovation Index ranking
sections.summary: The Bloomberg Innovation Index ranked Singapore as the third most innovative economy in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Bloomberg Innovation Index has ranked Singapore as the third most innovative economy in the world.

sections.label: A*STAR industry projects and licences
sections.summary: Between 2011 and 2016, A*STAR worked on over 12,000 industry projects, attracted over $2 billion in research investments, and its cumulative licence adoption more than doubled from 191 in 2014 to 422 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Between 2011 and 2016, A*STAR worked on more than 12,000 industry projects, attracting more than $2 billion in research investments from companies through joint collaborations and other open innovation platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In addition, with favourable licensing terms for local enterprises and the introduction of simplified licensing processes in 2013, the cumulative adoption of A*STAR licences has more than doubled from 191 in 2014 to 422 in 2016.

sections.label: University-industry licence agreements increase
sections.summary: Licence agreements between universities and industry rose from about 20 in 2010 to 95 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As a result of this industry alignment, we have seen an increase in the number of licence agreements between the universities and industry, from about 20 in 2010 to 95 in 2016.

sections.label: GIA office locations
sections.summary: GIA is now present in San Francisco, Jakarta, Bangkok and Beijing.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: GIA is now present in San Francisco, Jakarta, Bangkok and Beijing.

sections.label: Carbon tax rate and large emitters
sections.summary: Concerns about the carbon tax should be mitigated by the lower uniform rate of $5 per tonne from 2019 to 2023 and the focus on large emitters.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Mr Thomas Chua's understandable concerns about the impact of the carbon tax on businesses should be mitigated to some extent by the fact that we are starting with a lower uniform rate of $5 per tonne of emissions from 2019 to 2023, and we are focusing on the large emitters.

sections.label: Spending above expected carbon tax revenue
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance stated Singapore is prepared to spend more than the expected carbon tax revenue of nearly $1 billion in the initial five years to support projects delivering emissions abatement.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As the Minister for Finance has stated, we are prepared to spend more than the expected carbon tax revenue of nearly $1 billion in the initial five years to support worthwhile projects that deliver the required emissions abatement.

sections.label: OEM start in Jurong
sections.summary: OEM will commence in Jurong on 1 April with about 120,000 households and small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: OEM will commence in Jurong on 1 April, with about 120,000 households and small businesses.

sections.label: Jurong soft launch feedback
sections.summary: The Jurong soft launch lets EMA, SP Group and retailers gather feedback and finetune processes before OEM extends to 1.3 million accounts in the second half of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, in other words, you also have a "do-nothing" option and things will just carry on as per normal.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This soft launch in Jurong will allow EMA, SP Group and retailers to gather feedback and finetune processes, before we continue extending the OEM to the remaining 1.3 million accounts, mostly households, in the second half of 2018.

sections.label: Enhanced EDG grant support
sections.summary: The new EDG will support companies of all sizes, with enhanced grant support of up to 70% for SMEs extended another two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The new EDG will support companies of all sizes in their growth journeys.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will extend the enhanced grant support of up to 70% for SMEs for another two years, instead of reverting to 50%.

sections.label: PSG grants and funding
sections.summary: PSG starts with a simplified application process and streamlined grants, with up to 70% funding support and raised, customised grant caps.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: PSG will start with a simplified application process and by streamlining at least three pre-scoped grants: SPRING Singapore's ICV, the National Parks Board’s Landscape Productivity Grant (LPG), and the Infocomm and Media Development Authority’s (IMDA's) support for pre-scoped solutions under the SMEs Go Digital Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Government will provide up to 70% funding support for PSG to help companies committed to transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To better support businesses with heavier investments for longer time commitments, the grant caps have also been raised and customised for each industry.

sections.label: BGP and LicenceOne counts
sections.summary: BGP presently hosts six grants across five agencies, and LicenceOne has 118 licences from 20 agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Presently, BGP hosts six grants across five agencies, and LicenceOne has 118 licences from 20 agencies.

sections.label: Consolidated LEAD programme
sections.summary: LEAD supported about 50 TAC-led projects impacting over 8,500 companies, and a consolidated enhanced LEAD programme is being introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In the past two years alone, LEAD has supported some 50 TAC-led projects, impacting more than 8,500 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Last year, LEAD was not only expanded to support a larger base of TACs, but the maximum support level was also increased from 70% to 90% to support multi-TAC high-impact projects, both within and across sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: TACs may be confused by the parallel programmes with some overlaps in areas, such as eligibility criteria, supportable activities scope, and funding support levels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We are, therefore, introducing a consolidated LEAD programme which will be enhanced to support a wider range of TAC-led projects.

sections.label: Food Innovation and Resource Centre
sections.summary: The Food Innovation and Resource Centre at Singapore Polytechnic supports food manufacturers in developing innovative new products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: One of our Centres of Innovation, the Food Innovation and Resource Centre (FIRC) at Singapore Polytechnic, supports food manufacturers in developing innovative new products.

sections.label: Lounge manhour savings
sections.summary: The lounge achieved manhour savings of up to 45% and staff welcomed the convenience of centralisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The lounge, once heavily-reliant on staff, achieved manhour savings of up to 45%, and its staff have welcomed the convenience of centralisation.

sections.label: Tourego retail outlets

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To date, over 150 retail outlets benefit from the use of Tourego.

sections.label: Design Orchard opening

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Design Orchard, jointly developed by STB, SPRING Singapore and JTC, will open by the end of this year.

sections.label: Heartland shops and HDB shops
sections.summary: Heartland shops are likely the most representative micro-enterprises, with more than 14,000 HDB shops in 15 town centres and 110 neighbourhood centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Heartland shops are probably the most representative form of micro-enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: There are more than 14,000 Housing and Development Board (HDB) shops in Singapore’s 15 town centres and 110 neighbourhood centres.

sections.label: Revitalisation of Shops Scheme
sections.summary: HDB's Revitalisation of Shops Scheme funds merchant associations to upgrade shopping environments and hold promotional events, with FMAS representing 41 associations and SPRING Singapore support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Furthermore, HDB’s Revitalisation of Shops Scheme provides funding for merchant associations to upgrade their shopping environment and carry out promotional events to attract crowds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Federation of Merchants' Associations, Singapore (FMAS) is a collection of these associations and currently represents 41 merchants' and hawkers' associations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Its efforts are supported by SPRING Singapore through a LEAD project, which includes funding for a consultancy study and secondment of a public officer to FMAS.

sections.label: Encouraging TAC leadership roles
sections.summary: The speaker encourages people to take TAC leadership roles and thanks existing TAC leaders for their service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: If you are, I encourage you to consider stepping up to take a leadership role.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: And if you are already a TAC leader, I would like to thank you for your service and encourage you to continue working with partners to bring transformation to your industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Together, we can build a strong business ecosystem that will benefit all workers and enterprises in Singapore and allow us to remain relevant and competitive in the future economy.

sections.label: Government support for sector transformation
sections.summary: The Government is ready to support more companies with initiatives customised to each sector, highlighting manufacturing and wholesale trade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Some companies have already moved to transform their businesses and are today enjoying the fruits of transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We want to help more companies seize these opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government is ready to support them with initiatives customised to each sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Some sectors I would like to highlight are the manufacturing and wholesale trade sectors.

sections.label: Sector GDP and employment share

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The sector accounts for around 20% of our GDP and around 14% of our total employment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In 2016, PE companies invested 50% more in R&D, compared to the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As of November 2017, A*STAR has engaged over 300 companies through OTR.

sentences.text: Since its launch in April last year, 45 solutions have been made available and more than 1,000 companies have adopted solutions from Tech Depot.

sections.label: Wholesale trade in Singapore
sections.summary: Wholesale trade accounts for about 16% of GDP and comprises over 35,000 firms in B2B transactions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Today, wholesale trade is a key contributor to Singapore’s economy, accounting for about 16% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Most have the misperception that it involves working in warehouses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It is one of our economy’s largest and most diverse sectors, comprising more than 35,000 firms engaging in Business-to-Business (B2B) transactions for a wide range of goods, ranging from household goods and consumer electronics to food items and commodities.

sections.label: Trade platform and TIDF

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In a mere five months, over 2,300 companies have joined the platform, with close to 4,000 transactions completed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To help strengthen our trade ecosystem, we will establish the Trade Infrastructure Development Fund (TIDF) this year.

sections.label: Singapore startup growth

sentences.text: The total number of startups in Singapore grew from 22,000 in 2003 to 43,000 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: They contributed $7.7 billion, or 1.9% of GDP in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In Singapore, the venture funding activity and deal flows have multiplied significantly from 80 deals worth US$136.4 million in 2012, to 174 deals worth US$1.37 billion in 2017.

sections.label: Co-investment partners for deep tech

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Building on this, SPRING Singapore appointed nine co-investment partners last month with the goal of further catalysing over $200 million into more deep tech startups in the growth sectors of Advanced Manufacturing and Engineering, Health and Biomedical Sciences, and Urban Solutions and Sustainability.

sections.label: CCS restructure and renaming

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To reflect its new role, CCS will be renamed the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS).

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The CPFTA protects consumers against errant retailers who engage in unfair trading practices, regardless of whether these transactions take place online or offline.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Government will study them and take them into account when we next review the relevant consumer protection legislations.

sentences.text: The Government is committed to helping Singaporeans build up international networks and cross-cultural awareness through market immersion and overseas training programmes.
